import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 1, 500)  # uniform time points from 0 to 1 second
x1 = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1.0 * t)  # a 1 Hz reference signal

clips.caption: First prepare the <c.aqua>time axis</c.aqua> and a 1 Hz reference <c.aqua>signal</c.aqua>.

actions.text: x_task = 0.6 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 1.0 * (t - 0.2))  # shrink the amplitude to 0.6 and shift right by 0.2 s

clips.caption: Scale the <c.aqua>amplitude</c.aqua> by 0.6 and move the whole waveform 0.2 s to the right with t-0.2.

actions.text:
plt.figure(figsize=(7, 3))
plt.plot(t, x1, label="x1")
plt.plot(t, x_task, label="0.6 * x1 shifted right by 0.2 s")
plt.title("Scale and time shift")
plt.xlabel("Time (s)")
plt.ylabel("Amplitude")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

clips.caption: Draw the original and the transformed <c.aqua>signal</c.aqua> together and check that both <c.aqua>amplitude</c.aqua> and position match.
One way to write it is 0.6 times sin(2π times 1 times (t minus 0.2)). Observe: the <c.aqua>amplitude</c.aqua> is 0.6, the waveform moves right, and the <c.aqua>period</c.aqua> is still one second.
